pages.text: Tagging and Transcription for Chinese Heritage Records | National Archives Top Skip to main content Tagging and Transcription for Chinese Heritage Records From 1882 to 1943 the United States Government severely curtailed immigration from China to the United States, passing a series of laws whose result was the documentation of international movements of many Chinese nationals. Certain Federal agencies were particularly active in enforcing the exclusion laws, including the Customs Service, the Immigration and Naturalization Service (INS), which in 2003, became the United States Citizenship and Immigration Service (USCIS), and the U.S. District Courts. Many of the records created to implement the Chinese exclusion laws are now in the custody of the National Archives and have been digitized. The records are a major resource for the study of Chinese immigration and Chinese-American travel, trade, and social history from the late-19th to mid-20th century. Because many documents relate to individual immigrants, they are invaluable for the study of Chinese and Chinese-American family history. For more information about these records, please visit us online at https://www.archives.gov/research/chinese-americans Please help us tag, comment, and transcribe these records for greater access. Taking a Major Step Towards X-ray Beams from Laser Plasma Accelerators Using electrons from a laser plasma accelerator, researchers have demonstrated a greater than 1000-fold gain with high reliability in a free-electron laser. Basic Energy Sciences November 12, 2026 Estimated Read Time min This graphic illustrates a measurement of the increase in pulse energy from the free-electron laser mechanism. Image courtesy of Department of Energy's Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory The Science Laser plasma accelerators (LPAs) use powerful laser pulses to create waves inside a plasma. In just a few centimeters, these waves can push electrons to very high energies. In contrast, traditional particle accelerators need metallic structures that are several kilometers long to reach the same energy levels. But laser plasma accelerators are hard to control. This has made it difficult to produce stable, high-quality electron beams. Recently, scientists made an important advance. They showed that these compact accelerators can produce electron beams good enough to reliably power a highly demanding tool called a free-electron laser. Taking Steps for Cleaner Air for Respiratory Virus Prevention Aug. 18, 2025 Español What to know Respiratory viruses can spread in the air you breathe, especially in indoor and crowded spaces. Taking steps for cleaner air helps lower harmful germs or viruses in the air, reducing your chances of respiratory illness. It is a core prevention strategy recommended for everyone to lower your risk for respiratory illnesses. Recommendation As possible, take steps for cleaner air. This can mean bringing in fresh outside air, purifying indoor air, or gathering outdoors. Virus particles do not build up in the air outdoors as much as they do indoors. How it works Some germs spread in the air between people. This happens more easily in indoor, crowded spaces with poor airflow. To reduce the risk of exposure, it helps to improve air quality by increasing airflow, cleaning the air with air purifiers, or opting to gather outdoors. Close TaoEngine's Diary 【有时间就来写写枞阳的一些事情】关于康居路 Posted by TaoEngine on 15 July 2026 in Chinese (China) (‪中文(中国大陆)‬) . osm的小伙伴们大家好，今天我无意中发现了osm可以写日记然后放在自己的首页中。有的小伙伴分析地区编辑完完整度，有的教大家正确使用地图标签。虽然我注册有三年多了但是论辈分还是个小老弟😂，那我就写写我比较擅长的东西，欸要不我就写写有关家乡的一些事好了哈 关于康居路 枞阳县枞阳镇旗山社区邻近枞阳县人民医院、银塘花苑与银塘星城这三个区域中间有一条三级道路，道路有花坛阻拦，两条单行道形式，双向四车道（高峰期两车道因为两边可以停车） 这条道路的命名其实非常迷，枞阳县地图与天地图将其命名为健康路，而枞阳县ZY-02银塘行政区规划文件与地名信息系统将其命名为康居路（商业地图通常采用后者）。这条路到底叫康居路还是健康路？ 其实我住的地方离这条路不远，所以经常在傍晚散步时走这条路。根据我的见解以及查阅对应文件的思路，这条路现阶段应该还是命名为康居路为好，至少26年8月之前还是得叫它康居路 1. 根据路灯管理局的路灯标签判断 26年初，县里开展《城市生命线》安全设备部署工作，在大街小巷安装了监测设备，同时县里也提及同日设立路灯管理所。随即4月份县里的每个路灯都贴上了标签，其中这条路的路灯被贴上康居路标签。这项工作是领先于枞阳县地图的制作的，可以认定当前这条道路仍为康居路 2. 根据枞阳县ZY-02银塘行政区规划文件中康居小区存在与否判断 在枞阳县地图中，康居路并未消失而是跑到了旗山小学与中海山水城的区域中间，而它的命名依据是因为附近有个小区名为康居山庄。但是无论是在枞阳县ZY-02银塘行政区规划文件中，还是在旗山社区服务站点地图中，这个不是小区，是银塘村的回迁房，经简单查阅县政府公开文档初步确认区域名为银塘安置地。真正现存的“康居山庄”在妇幼保健院旁边，不过叫康居家园。当然不排除小区未来改名的情况 其次那条路虽然在路灯管理所的标签、附近停车场名称以及路牌中没有给出详细名称，但是在枞阳县ZY-02银塘行政区规划文件中，这条路被命名为安置地路。鉴于规划文件的审图号较枞阳县地图较新，该未分级道路我建议命名为安置地路，而保留原先的康居路命名位置 为啥要写这条路 上次有个过于热心的小伙伴将康居路所在道路标为健康路（与此同时他还把旗山路标为莲城路，而莲城路是天地图的一处过时标记，我有时间在下一次日记里说），希望我的笔记能在我没时间贡献枞阳的时候，给其他人一些有理可循的参考（与此同时我也会夹带一些私货介绍枞阳有什么有意思的地方，比如枞阳中学占据的地方曾经有个自然村叫答咀村，这个村的来历可神奇了，另开一个新坑），望大家多多关照👋 Location: 殷家老屋, 枞阳县, 枞阳镇, 枞阳县, 铜陵市, 安徽省, 246700, 中国 Discussion Comment from TaoEngine on 18 November 2026 at 04:59 打脸了，旗山小学那条路今天立牌子了😭就是康居路，马上改 Leave a comment Log in to leave a comment

A common scam geared towards tax pros aims to collect their Electronic Filing Identification Numbers. How the scam works The scammer poses as a tax software provider and emails the tax pro with a request to provide their EFIN information by fax. When the tax pro faxes back their EFIN information, the scammer uses the information to steal client data and file fraudulent tax returns for refunds. The team managed to electronically tag 10 of them and the largest was 60cm (23ins) in length and weighted 435g (0.9lbs). Ward said: "European eels start to migrate downstream during autumn and winter, when river discharges increase. pages.description: Nikkolas Smith, the bestselling illustrator, has a new children's book that takes a look at the innovative, creative dawn of our species.
pages.text: Telling the story of humanity’s origins in Africa—this time, for kids | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE Telling the story of humanity’s origins in Africa—this time, for kids Nikkolas Smith, the bestselling illustrator, has a new children's book that takes a look at the innovative, creative dawn of our species. The illustrator Nikkolas Smith, surrounded by his original canvas paintings for his new children's book, The History of We. Photograph By Vanessa Crocini By Kyndall Cunningham Published June 11, 2025 You’ve probably heard that we can all trace our roots back to Africa. It’s a fact that most people learn about briefly in a history class or find out through 23andMe. Still, this shared origin story often feels like a blip in our consciousness compared to other time periods. It’s a commonality we’re willing to acknowledge but not always explore. Picture-book author and film illustrator Nikkolas Smith fills in this curiosity gap with his latest book, The History of We , which he both wrote and illustrated. The self-described “artivist” has dedicated much of his career to rendering crucial moments and people in Black history through expressive paintings, from portraits of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor to a comic-book treatment of the Obamas. One of his most well-known projects is The 1619 Project: Born on the Water, the children’s adaptation of the New York Times venture led by Nikole-Hannah Jones, which he illustrated. With The History of We , Smith continues this tradition of documenting Black history in a way that’s accessible, honest, and completely mesmerizing.

Humans have been raising turkeys for thousands of years. Although indigenous peoples in North America have hunted wild turkeys since the end of the last Ice Age, the animals were first domesticated in Mexico around 2,000 years ago. Dinner wasn’t the original goal: archaeological evidence suggests turkeys were initially kept so their feathers could be used in clothing and ceremonial regalia. By A.D. 500, people were raising turkeys in what is now the United States too, judging by archaeological remains from caves in Arizona and New Mexico. Even so, those weren’t the birds that English settlers ate in the Thirteen Colonies. The domestic turkey descends from a southern Mexican bird that the Spanish took home in the 1500s. The birds then spread through Europe, and colonists brought them back across the Atlantic. The bird’s English name may reflect this long-distance trade: turkeys are thought to have reached England along winding trading routes that first passed through the country of Turkey. 2. Residents used pots and pans to clear water from their flooded tents, with some saying they were left without shelter. Jonathan Veitch, the Unicef representative for Palestine, said the "desperate" situation was being made worse by Israeli restrictions on the entry of heavy machinery and supplies such as engine oil. Some 90% of Gaza residents have been displaced by the Israeli war against Hamas, many of them multiple times, with limited access to clean water and sanitation. Aid agencies say the situation is likely to worsen with the start of the rainy season. Speaking to the BBC from Deir Al Balah in central Gaza, Veitch said: "It's just horrific and they're absolutely desperate. Testing for Hepatitis B For Everyone Nov. 2, 2026 Key points Getting tested for hepatitis B is the only way to find out if you are infected. All adults and pregnant women should get tested for hepatitis B. People with ongoing risk need periodic testing. You can find out if you have hepatitis B through a blood test. Why get tested Many people with hepatitis B do not look or feel sick, so testing is the only way to know if you are infected. It's important to get tested for hepatitis B, so that if you are infected you can get medical care and avoid spreading the virus to others. Chronic, or long-term, hepatitis B can cause serious health problems, including liver damage, liver cancer, liver failure, and even death. Tetanus: Causes and How It Spreads For Everyone Sept. 10, 2026 Español Key points Tetanus spores from the environment enter the body through cuts or wounds. Tetanus doesn't spread from person to person. It is possible to have tetanus infection more than once. Prevent tetanus by staying up to date with vaccinations and seeking appropriate care after a wound. Causes Bacteria live in the environment Spores of Clostridium tetani are common in the environment, including soil, dust, and manure. The spores develop into bacteria when they enter the body. Common exposures The spores can get into someone's body through broken skin, usually through injuries. Tetanus bacteria are more likely to infect certain breaks in the skin, including: Wounds contaminated with dirt, feces (poop), or saliva (spit) Puncture wounds (wounds caused by an object, like a nail or needle) Injuries with dead tissue (e.g., burns, crush injuries, frostbite) Dead tissue is a concern because it can promote bacteria growth. pages.title: Thawing Permafrost May Have Created a New Type of Landslide, Which Could Become More Common as the World Warms
pages.description: Scientists call the events permafrost detachment slides. Instead of thawing from the top down, these landslides seem to originate from a weakened base
pages.text: Thawing Permafrost May Have Created a New Type of Landslide, Which Could Become More Common as the World Warms Skip to main content A scar left by the 2018 Redstone River permafrost landslide, one of the two events investigated in the new study. Adapted from J. M. Young et al., Geophysical Research Letters , 2026 In 2017 and 2018, a pair of strange landslides moved huge masses of rock and dirt in Canada’s Northwest Territories. The events occurred in the central Mackenzie Valley, and one of them even dammed a river and created a lake . The two natural disasters are part of a new class of landslides scientists are calling “permafrost detachment slides” in a study published in the journal Geophysical Research Letters in September. They may have been partially triggered by severe wildfires that occurred in 1995, which destabilized the ground and allowed the base of the permafrost to thaw. What’s more, these events may become more common as the planet continues to warm. “It’s a very dramatic manifestation of the changing climate,” says study co-author Joseph Young , a geoscientist who conducted the work at the University of Alberta in Canada, to Matt Simon at Grist . “They’ve only started happening in the last 10, 15 years, and it’s a very drastic and abrupt change in the landscape.” Young and his colleagues began the study after seeing something strange in the Northwest Territories in 2019. While conducting field research, they spotted large landslide scars in valleys that they knew were stable permafrost , or permanently frozen earth, reports Stephanie Pappas for Live Science

pages.description: The discovery carries intense personal meaning for an Alabama community of descendants of the ship's survivors
pages.text: The 'Clotilda,' the Last Known Slave Ship to Arrive in the U.S., Is Found Skip to main content The descendants of Cudjo Lewis and Abache (above) heard stories of the ship that tore their ancestors from their homeland and now the wreck of the Clotilda has been confirmed to be found in Alabama's Mobile River. Wikimedia Commons One hundred and fifty-nine years ago, slave traders stole Lorna Gail Woods ’ great-great grandfather from what is now Benin in West Africa. Her ancestor, Charlie Lewis, was brutally ripped from his homeland, along with 109 other Africans, and brought to Alabama on the Clotilda , the last known slave ship to arrive in the United States. Today, researchers confirmed that the remains of that vessel, long rumored to exist but elusive for decades, have been found along the Mobile River, near 12 Mile Island and just north of the Mobile Bay delta. “The excitement and joy is overwhelming,” says Woods, in a voice trembling with emotion. She is 70 years old now. But she’s been hearing stories about her family history and the ship that tore them from their homeland since she was a child in Africatown, a small community just north of Mobile founded by the Clotilda ’s survivors after the Civil War. The authentication and confirmation of the Clotilda was led by the Alabama Historical Commission and SEARCH Inc., a group of maritime archaeologists and divers who specialize in historic shipwrecks. With pretty much every available television slot now exhausted, next year the Premier League and the EFL are set to hold serious discussions about its future. There are concerns, especially within non-league football, that removing the blackout could have detrimental effects on attendances and finances. Prime Minister Andy Burnham agrees, urging caution and suggesting the health of the football pyramid should come first . But many Premier League fans feel they are short-changed, locked out of many of their team's fixtures just because they live in this country. Go anywhere else in the world, and every single match is available live. With streaming so prevalent, to some the blackout feels archaic. Yet it is a complex situation, and many feel the depth of English football's pyramid is like nowhere else. BBC Sport looks at the history of the blackout, why it is unique to British football and the arguments for and against keeping it.
